description: Springer Nature's journal class. Not on CTAN: sn-jnl.cls is from the publisher's journal article template package (December 2024), the zip its requirement document names. Options as the template's default (sn-article.tex:65): pdflatex only stops the class loading breakurl, which writes dvips PostScript. The class calls amsmath's \allowdisplaybreaks at \begin{document} and leaves loading amsmath to the document, as the template does. Two more preamble lines (batch 1, round 2, from GitHub run 41584963423): (1) the kernel's \cline (latex.ltx l.16972) is restored: sn-jnl.cls l.1321 lets \cline be booktabs' \cmidrule, which nothing has defined yet when the class loads, so \cline was undefined in every document ('Undefined control sequence \abShortLine ->\cline' in awesomebox's block, and arydshln saved the undefined \cline as \adl@org@cline). (2) \labelitemi leaves vertical mode first: sn-jnl.cls l.1118 makes it \raise1pt\hbox{\textbullet}, and \raise cannot start a paragraph, so an inline list (paralist's inparaitem) whose label began a paragraph stopped at 'You can't use \raise in vertical mode'. In a list's label box \leavevmode does nothing. A further line (b23 PG-3, from GitHub run r2-461ed0e): in a document that loads multicol, TeX counts the footnote rule's height. sn-jnl's \footnoterule (sn-jnl.cls l.280-287, one column: \kern3pt, a 0.2mm rule, \kern5.5pt) takes 9.07pt, where LaTeX's convention, which TeX's page builder and multicol's column height (\leave@mult@footins, multicol.sty l.500-503: \skip\footins and the notes' height only) both rely on, is a rule that takes none. multicol fills its columns to the exact height, so a page it made with a footnote ran past the text block (11.46907pt with the last note's depth, which \maxdepth 0pt, l.274, adds): a document problem in 14 sn-jnl.A cells (782 not-denied rows) and a branch's own in 20 (64 rows), every one holding multicol and a footnote; 729 rows failed on nothing else. At \begin{document} the line measures the rule, adds its height to \skip\footins and starts the rule with a kern of the same amount back up, so the rule and the notes print where they did, and the page builder and multicol leave the room they take (GitHub probe b23-1, df1e5ff8db1fb0ec2bf31: 11.46907pt became 2.40002pt, the last note's depth, within the tolerance, and all 56 branches without an overfull box of their own pass). A document without multicol keeps both as the class sets them. One more line (b23, ERRORS H-SNJNL), the first of the preamble, for pinned floats ([H]): sn-jnl's table environment wraps the kernel's (sn-jnl.cls l.1326-1340: \begin{tableorg}[#1], then center and threeparttable), and float.sty's [H] lets \end<type> be its own end (float.sty v1.3d l.78-79: \expandafter\let\csname end#1\endcsname\float@endH, #1 the float type), so a table[H] lost sn-jnl's \end{threeparttable}\end{center}\end{tableorg} and stopped at 'Extra }, or forgotten \endgroup' in \@endfloatbox and '\begin{threeparttable} on input line N ended by \end{table}', then \end{document} in internal vertical mode (GitHub run r2-461ed0e: dcf84729ee01639026a27 l.878, 73 failing not-denied branches; General prints [H] for a pinned table or figure, positioning fixed). When float.sty loads, its \@float@HH is replaced by a copy that lets the end of the environment being begun, \@currenvir, be \float@endH: the same as before for a float begun directly (\begin{table}[H], \begin{figure}[H]), and sn-jnl's tableorg for its wrapped table, whose own end code then closes threeparttable and center first.
